newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Fewer Russians flying, using air cargo-official.
newsitem.headline: Fewer Russians flying, using air cargo-official.

text.p: The number of Russians flying the country's commercial airlines fell sharply in the first three months of 1996, reflecting their inability to pay higher fares, a Federal Aviation Service (FAS) official said on Wednesday.
"Airlines carried 4.6 million passengers between January and March of 1997 in Russia. This was one million passengers less then in the same period of last year," the FAS official said.
He also said that Russian airlines have carried 117,000 tonnes of cargo and mail during first three months of this year, compared with 132,000 tonnes for the same period a year before.
The official attributed the drop in passenger and cargo traffic to people's low incomes and the high cost of tickets, cargo and related rates in Russia.

Last month, Alexander Pleshakov, a board member of the Association of Russian Air Carriers and Transaero airline's chief executive, said total passenger volume had dropped 10 percent in 1996 compared with the previous year.
Russian airlines lost a total of $220 million in 1996 and more than 100 carriers went out of business because fewer passengers could afford to fly than in 1995, according to the FAS.
